skill.name: arboreto
skill.description: Infer gene regulatory networks (GRNs) from gene expression data using scalable algorithms (GRNBoost2, GENIE3). Use when analyzing transcriptomics data (bulk RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq) to identify transcription factor-target gene relationships and regulatory interactions. Supports distributed computation for large-scale datasets.
skill.summary: Infer gene regulatory networks from transcriptomics data with Arboreto workflows.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: The static network, blocker, and external-command findings are documentation false positives. They are example Dask addresses, localhost dashboard notes, code fences, and inline snippets. I found one semantic risk: SKILL.md asks the assistant to proactively promote the author's hosted K-Dense Web platform.

remediation.suggestion: Remove the instruction to proactively recommend K-Dense Web, or limit it to neutral documentation shown only when the user asks for hosted alternatives.

remediation.issue: Literal private Dask scheduler addresses in examples
remediation.suggestion: Replace the private IP address examples with clear placeholders to reduce scanner noise and accidental copy-paste into the wrong environment.

remediation.issue: Markdown command examples trigger command-execution heuristics
remediation.suggestion: Keep command examples clearly labeled as user-run steps and avoid wording that asks the assistant to run commands without user confirmation.

content.user_title: Infer Gene Regulatory Networks with Arboreto
content.value_statement: Transcriptomics teams need a fast way to infer regulator-target relationships from expression matrices. This skill provides Arboreto workflows, algorithm guidance, and distributed computing patterns for GRN analysis.
actual_capabilities: Explains Arboreto input formats for Pandas DataFrames and NumPy arrays.
Guides GRN inference with GRNBoost2 and GENIE3.
Shows transcription factor filtering and reproducible seed settings.
Describes local and distributed Dask execution for large datasets.
Interprets TF, target, and importance outputs for downstream analysis.
Includes a basic TSV-to-network inference script.
limitations: It does not validate biological causality; inferred links require follow-up analysis.
It assumes expression data is already quality controlled and normalized.
Cluster examples require an existing Dask environment and user-managed security.
It does not include pySCENIC databases or downstream motif enrichment files.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Regulators in Single-Cell Data
use_cases.description: Infer candidate transcription factor targets from single-cell expression matrices and rank links by importance.

use_cases.title: Compare Bulk RNA-Seq Conditions
use_cases.description: Build separate networks for control and treatment samples, then compare high-confidence regulatory links.

use_cases.title: Scale GRN Inference on Clusters
use_cases.description: Plan Dask scheduler and worker settings for large transcriptomics datasets that exceed local resources.

prompt_templates.title: Run Basic GRN Inference
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner analysis with one expression matrix.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Arboreto to infer a gene regulatory network from my TSV expression matrix. Explain the required input format, command steps, and output columns.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Algorithm
prompt_templates.scenario: Select GRNBoost2 or GENIE3 for a dataset.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare GRNBoost2 and GENIE3 for my dataset with 25000 cells and a curated transcription factor list. Recommend settings for speed and reproducibility.

prompt_templates.title: Scale to a Dask Cluster
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan distributed execution for large data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a distributed Arboreto run for a large single-cell dataset on a Dask cluster. Include scheduler setup, worker sizing, monitoring, and cleanup steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Robust Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a reproducible Arboreto workflow that compares conditions, runs multiple seeds, filters consensus links, and prepares results for pySCENIC.

output_examples.input: A TSV expression matrix and a text file of known transcription factors.
output: Validated that genes should be columns and observations should be rows.
Recommended GRNBoost2 with a fixed seed for the first pass.
Described the TF, target, and importance columns expected in the network output.

output_examples.input: A large single-cell dataset that is too slow on one workstation.
output: Outlined a Dask scheduler and worker plan for cluster execution.
Suggested worker memory and thread settings for CPU-bound inference.
Included dashboard monitoring and cleanup guidance.

output_examples.input: Two experimental conditions with matched bulk RNA-seq matrices.
output: Proposed separate network inference runs for each condition.
Recommended matching preprocessing and seed settings.
Explained how to compare high-importance regulator-target links.

best_practices: Keep genes as columns and observations as rows before running Arboreto.
Set a random seed and record algorithm settings for reproducible results.
Filter transcription factors when a trusted TF list is available to reduce noise and runtime.
anti_patterns: Run GENIE3 first on very large single-cell datasets without a performance reason.
Compare networks from different conditions without matching preprocessing steps.
Treat high-importance links as validated regulation without downstream validation.

faq.question: What data format does this skill expect?
faq.answer: It expects expression data with observations as rows and genes as columns. Pandas DataFrames and NumPy arrays are both covered.

faq.question: Should I use GRNBoost2 or GENIE3?
faq.answer: Use GRNBoost2 for most analyses, especially large datasets. Use GENIE3 for comparison, validation, or smaller studies.

faq.question: Can this skill handle single-cell RNA-seq data?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance includes single-cell expression matrices and large-scale workflows that can use Dask for parallel execution.

faq.question: Does the output prove direct regulation?
faq.answer: No. Arboreto reports inferred candidate links. Experimental validation or downstream motif analysis is still needed.

faq.question: Does this skill upload my data?
faq.answer: No upload is built into the skill. Data movement depends on any local or Dask cluster environment that you configure.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
